Epistemic Grounding: The Dualistic Nature of Types, Class Representability, and Expressions
Notation is fragile—always consult program/types/typetheory.ML for semantics rather than surface syntax. In Obelisk, we rigorously disambiguate four foundational principles:
  • 1. The Dualistic (at least!) Nature of Types (Syntactic AST vs. Semantic Predicate on Classes): Every type in typetheory.ML has at least a dualistic nature: (a) Syntactically, a type is an expression syntax tree (Small.Col.Expression or Huge.Col.Expression, constructed via OpSet, OpClass, OpFamily, OpConstructor); (b) Semantically, a type corresponds to a predicate on classes (LPredicate / Class -> Bool, via LTpEmb / Emb). Thus \( \mathrm{CLASS}(\mathrm{V}) \) is a well-formed mathematical formula inside the object theory, and in fact a theorem (\( \vdash \mathrm{CLASS}(\mathrm{V}) \), asserting that the universal class V satisfies the class predicate), which is distinct from the metalevel typing judgment (V : Class) or \( (\mathcal{W} : \mathsf{Theory}) \). Similarly, \( \mathrm{SET}(\emptyset) \) is a theorem, while \( \neg\mathrm{SET}(\mathrm{V}) \) is Russell's theorem.
  • 2. Types Representable by a Class vs. Proper Conglomerate Types (“When You Can Write Both : and ∈”):
    • Representable by a Class: Sometimes a type's semantic predicate holds only on sets belonging to a single class—for instance, Set is represented by the universal class V = {x | isSet(x)}, and syntactic datatypes of finite syntax trees (such as Class.Expression, Fm, Stmt, Prf) are representable by code classes in V_ω ⊂ V via Gödel encoding Enc. Because Class.Expression is a datatype of finite syntax trees (and representable by a class), for a class term expression t (such as \( (t = \langle x \rangle) \), the AST node embedding variable x) you can write both the typing judgment \( (t : \mathsf{Class.Expression}) \) and the membership formula \( (t \in \mathsf{Class.Expression}) \).
    • Not Representable by a Class (Proper Conglomerates): Other times, a type's predicate holds on proper classes (such as Class itself, where CLASS(X) ↔ ⊤). Its extension is a proper conglomerate (Huge.Col) that is not representable by any class in Morse–Kelley or NBG (since there is no class of all classes)—and that is completely fine! For a class variable x, you write the typing judgment \( (x : \mathsf{Class}) \) (or predicate CLASS(x)), but you cannot write x ∈ Class.
  • 3. The “Off-by-One” (Shift-to-Term, n → n+1) Level Rule & SML Kernel Type Glossary: Standard ML cannot store arbitrary mathematical classes or sets in memory; therefore level-0 mathematical sorts are uninhabited phantom types at SML runtime (type Class = Nonstored.t, type Set = Nonstored.t, where Nonstored.t = Void.t has no runtime values), and SML shifts every level n to level n+1 by storing syntactic expressions of those objects:
    • A.t = Nonstored.t: The abstract level-0 mathematical sort (e.g. Class.t, Truth.t, Theory.t), uninhabited at SML runtime.
    • A_Expre (Class_Expre, Fm_Expre = Truth_Expre, Theory_Expre): The SML head-constructor datatype (HC, HP, HA, HI) for compound expressions of sort A.
    • A.Expression.t = A_Expre sion: The full recursive SML AST wrapping A_Expre with metavariables (EVar), quotation (EInject), antiquotation (EAnti), evaluation (EEval), substitution (ESubst), and conditionals (EIf).
    • Fm = Truth.Expression.t and Ctx = XCtx of Fm list: Formula syntax trees and finite hypothesis contexts. Decidable side conditions on these ASTs are directly executable boolean functions in CakeML and Poly/ML.
  • 4. Turnstiles, Undecidable Provability vs. Decidable Proof Checking, & Theorems:
    • Exact Order of the Turnstile Relation: A sequent statement is written T, Γ ⊢ φ (or equivalently Γ ⊢_T φ): it is a ternary relation between Theory T (\(\mathcal{T} : \mathsf{Theory}\)), Context Γ (\(\Gamma : \mathsf{Ctx}\)), and Formula φ (\(\phi : \mathsf{Fm}\)), represented in the SML kernel by Stmt_p = ApStmt of Theory * Ctx * Fm.
    • Why Provability is Undecidable while Proof Checking is Decidable: Existential provability (∃(p : Prf), p : ProofOf(T, Γ ⊢ φ), i.e. whether there exists a proof of φ from T, Γ) is undecidable in general: for consistent finitely axiomatized theories extending Robinson arithmetic (including τ_NBG and τ_MK) it is Σ^0_1-complete by Church–Turing–Gödel; for higher-order subsystem F it is Δ^1_1-hard; and for an arbitrary semantic theory parameter W : Theory (which may be uncountable or non-r.e.) it is not even recursively enumerable. By contrast, proof verification (checking whether a given proof term p : Prf witnesses statement s : Stmt, i.e. Enc(p) ∈ ProofsOf(Enc(s))) is primitive recursive and decidable.
    • Material Implication (→) vs. Sequent Turnstile (⊢): Object-level material implication (→, constructor TpImpl : Fm * Fm -> Fm) is a truth-functional connective inside formulas (Fm), whereas the turnstile (⊢, constructor ApStmt : Theory * Ctx * Fm -> Stmt) is the sequent judgment constructor forming a Stmt. Turnstiles (⊢) must never be used where material implication (→) is intended.
    • Statement vs. Theorem (Syntactical Variant 1, SML Kernel, & Semantical Variant 2): A Statement (s : Stmt) is a syntactic sequent T, Γ ⊢ φ. In the Syntactical Variant (Variant 1, 1st-Order), a Theorem is a dependent pair in the Sigma-type Σ(s : Stmt) ProofOf(s) (with ProofOf(s) / ProofsOf(Enc(s)) typing the proof witness), which is implemented in Standard ML as the algebraic datatype datatype Thm = Thm of Stmt.Expression * Prf. In the Semantical Variant (Variant 2, RoqC-style Higher-Order), a formula φ is a type directly, so a theorem is simply Theorem name : φ := prf without needing ProofOf.
    • Why ∀(T : Type) is Replaced by Metalevel Syntactic Quantification ∀(T_e : Type_Expression), ◃ … &llbracket;T_e&rrbracket; … ▹: In semantic MK/NBG class theory, quantifying over all semantic types (∀(T : Type)) is strictly forbidden because type Type = Nonstored.t has no semantic carrier class (avoiding Girard’s / Russell’s paradox). Therefore, type-polymorphic rules (such as 3.23 simple_if, 3.24 if_dep, 4.01, and 4.02) quantify on the metalevel over syntactic type expressions ∀(T_e : Type_Expression) and wrap the object-level formula in type-quotation brackets ◃ … &llbracket;T_e&rrbracket; … ▹ (or angle-bar brackets ⟨| … [|T_e|] … |⟩), where &llbracket;T_e&rrbracket; unquotes/evaluates the syntactic type expression T_e into a semantic type inside the quoted formula. Use the Type Quantification switch below to toggle between these notations.
Mathematical Architecture: Semantic Formulas, Side Conditions (NFV & FFI), and Catalog Conventions

In the Obelisk Proof Assistant, mathematical set/class semantics and syntactic metalevel side conditions are formally and rigorously decoupled:

  • The Two Real Interpretations (Set/Class Model vs. Executable SML Code): We strictly distinguish between (1) Meaning in Model inside MK/NBG (pure mathematical assertions: \( \forall X \), \( \forall (x \in \mathrm{V}) \), \( \mathrm{isSet}(x) \), avoiding any pseudo-membership like ∈ Theory or ∈ Class), and (2) Checkable / Executable Code in CakeML and Poly/ML (Standard ML AST expressions: Class_Expre, Fm_Expre, Theory_Expre, Ctx). Use the Interpretation switch in the header to view either representation.
  • Metatheoretic Variables \( (v_x, v_y, v_C, v_s) \) vs. Metatheoretic Constants \( (c_x, c_y, c_C) \) vs. Italic Red Class Variables & Upright Theory Symbols: When an arbitrary object-language variable is reasoned about schematically in a rule or side condition (such as \( (\mathrm{NFV}(v_C, \phi) = \mathrm{True}) \) or \( (\mathrm{FFI}(t, v_x, \phi) = \mathrm{True}) \)), it is represented by a metatheoretic variable \( (v_x : \mathsf{Variable}) \) in \( (v_x, v_y, v_C, v_s) \) (universally quantified on the metalevel over variable identifiers). By contrast, a fixed concrete variable identifier (such as Variable_id("x")) is denoted by a metatheoretic constant in \( (c_x, c_y, c_C) \). Constants (V for the universal class of all sets, On, ∅), functional symbols (ifdep, simple_if, sss, π1, π2), predicate symbols (isSet, isClassFunction, isUniverse, NFV, FFI), and theory symbols in general are rendered upright (not italicized), whereas class variables (\( X, Y, C, x, y, z \)) are rendered italicized in red (#f87171). When a formula makes sense specifically when a class variable denotes a set (for example on the left of ∈ or guarded by isSet(x)), we use lowercase (\( x, y, z, a, b, u, v \)) as a clean human-readable naming convention (never used by algorithms to decide semantics or typing).
  • Definitions of Decidable Side-Condition Predicates (NFV, FFI, Fresh):
    • NFV(v_x, φ) = True (“Not a Free Variable”): Variable identifier v_x does not occur free in formula AST φ (i.e. v_x ∉ FV(φ)), implemented by structural recursion in program/types/typetheory.ML and reflected in metatheory.html#nfv-prop.
    • FFI(t, v_x, φ) = True (“Free For Instantiation / Free For Substitution”): Term expression t is free for v_x in formula φ—no free variable of t becomes captured by any quantifier (∀, ∃) or class comprehension binder ({ z | ... }) when substituting t for free occurrences of v_x in φ (reflected in metatheory.html#ffi-quant).
    • Fresh(v_y, v_x) = True: Variable identifiers v_y and v_x are syntactically distinct (v_y ≠ v_x).
  • Formula Taxonomy (2×2 Terminology Switch), MK vs. NBG Switch, & Canonical entries.ML Numbering:
    • Terminology Switch (Row 1 below): Toggles between two standard naming conventions for closed vs. parameterized formulas: Mode A (Default) calls closed formulas without metavariables Formula and parameterized templates Formula Scheme; Mode B calls closed formulas Unschematic Formula and parameterized templates Formula.
    • Object Theory Switch (Row 2 below — MK vs. NBG): The kernel parameterizes class comprehension (3.01) by a boolean flag check_flag in program/types/foundations.ML: setting check_flag = true selects Morse–Kelley (τ_MK) (impredicative comprehension over arbitrary formulas), while check_flag = false enforces von Neumann–Bernays–Gödel (τ_NBG) (predicative comprehension restricted to set-quantified formulas).
    • Canonical entries.ML Item Numbering: Catalog item numbers (1.01–1.07, 2.01–2.05, 3.01–3.71) preserve the exact index positions in entries_list of program/types/entries.ML. Intermediate numbers between major axioms are conservative helper definitions (such as 3.02 ⊆, 3.08 isSet, 3.13 ∅, 3.15 ∩, 3.17 ∪, 3.20 {a,b}, 3.33 𝒫(a) Power Class Definition before 3.34 Power Set Axiom, and 3.37 Axiom of Replacement).

▸ Note

Unified Multi-Variant Architecture & Dual Semantics

Two Proof Assistant Variants, Decoupled Operators (Enc / Dec / Emb), and Option B Anatomy

Variant Bridge Verified (Poly/ML + CakeML)

Obelisk maintains two co-existing proof assistant variants in dedicated subdirectories of set_theory_prover/variants/, connected by an executable bidirectional translation bridge (program/variant_bridge.ML) and grounded in the dual semantics of program/types/typetheory.ML:

1. Variant 1 — Syntactical Proof Assistant (1st-Order, with ProofOf)
Open Dedicated Variant 1 Page →
Location: variants/variant1_first_order/ (newchecker.ML, types/typetheory.ML, types/foundations.ML)
Core Principle: Explicit syntactic datatypes (Fm, Ctx, Theory, Stmt, Prf) for 1st-order MK Class Theory statements about classes. Because statements (s : Stmt) are syntax trees (⟨...⟩ / ⟦...⟧) rather than ambient types, connecting a proof term to the statement it proves requires ProofOf / ProofsOf: (p : ProofOf(s)) (and via Gödel encoding Enc, (Enc(p) ∈ ProofsOf(Enc(s))) and (Enc(s) ∈ Theorems)).
2. Variant 2 — Semantical Proof Assistant (RoqC / Higher-Order)
Open Dedicated Variant 2 Page →
Location: variants/variant2_higher_order/ (nbg_compiler.ML, nbg_surface_compiler.ML, dependent_eval.ML)
Core Principle: RoqC / Curry–Howard dependent type theory where propositions/formulas are types directly (Theorem name : φ, prf : φ): implications are function spaces, quantifiers are dependent products/sums, and proofs are constructive λ-terms—no ProofOf wrapper or quotation brackets ⟨...⟩ needed.
Decoupled Brackets (⟨...⟩ / ⟦...⟧) vs. Special Functional Symbols (Enc, Dec, Emb)
  • Quotation ⟨...⟩ (<|...|>) & Antiquotation ⟦...⟧ ([|...|]): Purely syntax-splicing brackets. Inside ⟨...⟩, antiquoting a class variable ⟦X⟧ splices the class X itself—which may be a proper class like V or On! Therefore, isSet(⟦X⟧) is NOT automatically true (e.g. ¬isSet(V) by Russell's theorem).
  • Syntactic Encoding Enc(s) (CpEnc in typetheory.ML): Maps any syntactic object (s : T) (Fm, Stmt, Prf, Ctx, Theory) to its finite Gödel/hereditarily-finite set code in (V_ω ⊂ V). Because every finite syntax tree code is a finite set, isSet(Enc(s)) IS unconditionally true!
  • Syntactic Decoding Dec(c, T) (VDec in typetheory.ML): Partially decodes a set code (c : Class) back into target syntactic collection (T : Col), satisfying the roundtrip law ∀(s : T) (Dec(Enc(s), T) = s).
  • Dual Type Embedding Emb(T) (LTpEmb / TyTpEmb in typetheory.ML): Captures the Dual Semantics of typetheory.ML: (A) Semantic Predicate Interpretation: (Emb(Class)(X) ⟷ ⊤) (so Emb(Class)(V) is a theorem!) and (Emb(Set)(X) ⟷ isSet(X)) (so ¬Emb(Set)(V) is Russell's theorem); (B) Syntactic Code-Class Interpretation: for syntactic types (T ∈ {Fm, Stmt, Prf, Ctx, Theory}), (Emb(T)(x) ⟷ (x ∈ CodeClass(T))), where (CodeClass(T) = { c | (isSet(c) ∧ ∃(s : T) (c = Enc(s))) }).
Canonical Parameterized Axiom Anatomy — ax_A1(α : Fm, β : Fm)
1) (A1_fm(α : Fm, β : Fm) : Fm) :=
     (⟨((⟦α⟧ → (⟦β⟧ → ⟦α⟧)) : Bool)⟩ : Fm)   |   ⊤
2) (ctx_A1 : Ctx) := ([] : Ctx)
3) (theory_A1 : Theory) := (τ_MK : Theory)
4) (ax_A1(α : Fm, β : Fm) : Stmt) :=
     (⟨⟦theory_A1⟧, ⟦ctx_A1⟧ ⊢ ⟦A1_fm(α, β)⟧⟩ : Stmt)
5) (A1_prf(α : Fm, β : Fm) : Prf) :=
     (⟨fn hA => fn hB => hA⟩ : Prf)
6) ∀(α : Fm) ∀(β : Fm)
     (Enc(A1_prf(α, β)) ∈ ProofsOf(Enc(ax_A1(α, β))))
7) ∀(α : Fm) ∀(β : Fm)
     ((Enc(ax_A1(α, β)) ∈ Theorems) ⟷
      (∃(p : Class) (p ∈ ProofsOf(Enc(ax_A1(α, β))))))
Canonical 7-Part Option B Theorem Anatomy — thm_russell_not_set
1) (fm_russell_not_set : Fm) :=

Each row is a closed proof term in examples/nbg_verified_programs.nbg, compiled by NBGSurfaceCompiler (Variant 2 — Semantical / RoqC, where a formula φ is a type directly: Theorem name : φ) and automatically translated by VariantBridge into a 7-part Option B 1st-order NBG certificate (Variant 1 — Syntactical / 1st-Order, where (thm : Stmt) is a syntax tree and verification uses ProofsOf and Theorems) in Poly/ML and CakeML.

The dependent-checker catalog is audited separately: 52 derived proofs, 21 conservative definitions (including Enc, Dec, Emb, ProofsOf, Theorems), and 7 irreducible MK axioms. Definitional and axiomatic witnesses are never counted as derived theorems, and the kernel rejects the untrusted PCheat_prf placeholder on every certified path.
